messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — after the merge landed (main @ abcde7) we're seeing a clear ~35% p95 decode latency regression on short-sequence traffic. Canary traffic spiked around the merge window.

elaine: Which workloads? shortseq only or longseq too?

sanjay: Short-seq (seq<=16) is worst. Long seq looks fine. Quick perf numbers from canary logs: 
```
baseline (pre-merge): p50=28ms p95=62ms p99=120ms
HEAD (post-merge): p50=30ms p95=84ms p99=132ms
relative: p95 +35% (~22ms)
```

mike: I repro locally with the small harness. Command I ran: `./bench/bench_tool --model redwood-small --seq 8 --batch 4 --iters 500 --mode decode`

mike: attaching a microprofile snapshot (summarized): 
```
GPU kernel times (avg per token):
- attn_v2_fused: 0.18ms (used 70% of calls)
- attn_matmul_fallback: 0.55ms (used 30%, but dominates p95)
- kv_write memcpy: +0.12ms on eviction spikes
```

sanjay: Important note: kernel_selector is preferring the new attn_v2_fused for many cases, but for short batches it's flipping to attn_matmul_fallback in the middle of sequences which causes extra memcpy churn and KV cache evictions. Looks like a heuristic threshold regression.

kevin: That sounds like the fused-op reorder change from PR #4226 — it introduced a different ranking when batch_size*seq < threshold. cc @elaine for bisect.

elaine: Bisected: ACL 1. merge 2023-11-14 22:30 UTC -> PR #4226 is the first bad commit. It touched fused op scoring and prefetch ordering.

perf-bot: CI perf job perf-suite/shortseq/p95 FAILED at 2023-11-15T01:12:07Z (regression detected compared to baseline).

alex: Quick mitigation attempt: force kernel_selector to prefer attn_v1 for seq<=16 by setting env flag `KERNEL_FORCE_ATTNV1_SHORTSEQ=true` in canary. Patch diff: 
```
// runtime/selector/config.cc
if (env::get("KERNEL_FORCE_ATTNV1_SHORTSEQ") == "true" && seq <= 16) {
  prefer("attn_v1");
}
```

mike: I deployed that to canary and re-ran bench: new numbers: p50=31ms p95=72ms p99=125ms. p95 improved ~12ms vs HEAD, but p50 regen small.

sanjay: Nice — reduces the p95 delta by ~55%. Still not ideal long-term but acceptable as a short-term canary hold.

rachel: Recommend hold rollout and revert PR #4226 until follow-up fix for the selector heuristics. We should open a targeted follow-up to make heuristics stable across (batch, seq) domain and add unit tests.

kevin: Agreed. Also adding a deterministic kernel-selector unit test for seq=1..32, batch=1..8 to perf-suite so CI will catch this.

opsbot: Rollout paused for release/2023-11-15: p95 > rollout-threshold. (automated).

elaine: Filed issue #5432: "selector: fused-op scoring causes shortseq attn fallback and KV eviction thrash" with reproducer command and my bisect notes.

alex: Next steps: revert PR #4226 on main to stop the rest of the rollout, then a small follow-up PR to: 1) make selector deterministic for shortseq, 2) add microbench regression test, 3) add opt-in env flags for experiments.

mike: One extra datapoint: KV cache eviction metric 'kv.evictions/sec' jumped 2.4x on canary right after merge. That matches the memcpy spikes in the profile.

rachel: Okay — I'll approve the emergency revert and coordinate release ops. Post-merge we'll schedule a root-cause pairing session to harden fused-op heuristics. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: Thanks all. I'll keep the canary flag live and run a longer soak to watch p99.

perf-bot: Note: after revert candidate deploy, re-run perf-suite/shortseq and report within 1 hour.
